# Intake brief — Harvester enemy

**Headline:** Add a Harvester enemy archetype — a large, slow, roaming enemy
that actively seeks and absorbs the nearest mineral and survives five player
bullets — backed by data-driven regular-enemy health, wired into both the
shipped game and the enemy gym, and integrated into the campaign as a rare
roaming spawn.

## Problem statement

The bestiary currently has no enemy that competes with the player for
minerals. Non-asteroid enemies already absorb any mineral they happen to
overlap (GDD §4.4.1), but none deliberately hunts the field. The Harvester
introduces a mineral-denial threat: it actively drives to the nearest mineral,
is large (easy to hit and quick to absorb), slow to cross the screen, and
durable (five hits), forcing the player to spend ammunition and attention on it
before it strips the field.

## Users

- **As a player**, I want a durable enemy that actively steals minerals, so
  that collecting minerals becomes a contest rather than a free pickup.
- **As a player**, I want the Harvester to be large and slow, so that the
  five-hit cost is fair and readable rather than punishing.
- **As a designer**, I want to tune the Harvester (size, colour, speed,
  health, score) through the existing CSV/enemy-config pipeline without
  touching scene code.
- **As a developer**, I want multi-hit health and mineral seeking to be shared,
  data-driven capabilities, so future multi-hit or seeking enemies are cheap
  and the game and gyms cannot diverge.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — New `harvester` archetype is registered and discoverable.** A
  `harvester` row exists in `src/data/enemy-configs.csv` with a matching seed
  fallback in `src/core/configDefaults.ts`, is mapped in
  `src/entities/enemyFactory.ts`, appears in the gym index, and spawns/renders
  in `GymEnemies`. Regular-enemy health is data-driven: a `health` column is
  added to the CSV schema/codec (`src/core/csv.ts`) and `EnemyConfig`
  (`src/core/configTypes.ts`), defaulting to 1 so existing enemies are
  unchanged. Verified by config/CSV tests and a gym spawn test.
- [ ] **AC2 — Mineral-seeking behaviour.** The Harvester always steers toward
  the **nearest live mineral anywhere on the field** at its configured (slow)
  speed and absorbs it on overlap using the existing enemy-absorption rule
  (`collectMinerals`), incrementing its tracked mineral count. It does **not
  fire**, and it cannot take minerals from the player's hold. When no mineral
  exists it holds station / continues its idle drift. Verified by deterministic
  entity + scene tests that place minerals and assert the Harvester closes
  distance and consumes them, and that it fires no bullets.
- [ ] **AC3 — Five-hit destruction with readable feedback.** The Harvester has
  `health = 5` and survives exactly five player-bullet hits. Each non-lethal hit
  consumes the bullet and triggers the existing bullet-impact feedback; the
  fifth hit destroys it, plays destruction audio/VFX exactly once, awards
  **≈ 400** score, advances wave accounting, and re-drops 25–50 % of absorbed
  minerals per the existing rule. The shared multi-hit path must correctly
  finalise the kill (`onEnemyDestroyed`, destruction audio) — a gap that exists
  today. Verified by a five-hit test and a single-destruction/single-audio
  regression test.
- [ ] **AC4 — Existing enemies are unchanged.** All current 1-HP enemies
  (Scout, Diver, Tank, Phaser, Swarm, Asteroid) remain destroyed by one hit and
  their tests stay green.
- [ ] **AC5 — Game ↔ gym parity.** The Harvester's seek, absorption and
  five-hit destruction run through the same shared code path in `PlayScene` and
  in `GymEnemies` (per the gym-parity principle); no scene re-implements the
  behaviour.
- [ ] **AC6 — Campaign integration.** The Harvester is available in the gym
  **and** appears in the campaign as a rare roaming spawn in later levels
  (Levels 4–5), registered with the `WaveManager` so wave-clear accounting is
  correct. Verified by a wave/level test.
- [ ] **AC7 — Testing/validation.** New unit/integration tests cover: config
  codec round-trip (including the new `health` column), factory mapping, seek
  target selection (nearest mineral; none present), absorption counting,
  five-hit destruction, and a `PlayScene` + `GymEnemies` parity check. Full
  project test suite must pass with the new changes.
- [ ] **AC8 — Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect
  the changes, including the Game Design Document health model and enemy
  catalog (§2.3, §4.1, §4.4.1, §4.5, §6.5), the
  `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` catalog and add-an-enemy checklist
  (§1/§8), the README enemy list, and code comments.

## Constraints

- **Data-driven:** tuning lives in the CSV/enemy-config pipeline; no new
  per-enemy scene or hard-coded archetype branch.
- **Single source of truth:** no duplication of collision, mineral-collection,
  or health logic — this is a hard requirement of the gym-parity epic
  (`AH-0MUII2FJ5007MDDA`).
- **No regression:** existing 1-HP enemies and their tests must be untouched
  semantically; `health` defaults to 1.
- **GDD consistency:** the health-model change must be documented explicitly so
  the GDD no longer claims "all regular enemies are 1 HP"; P4 Bomb still deals
  **no** damage to enemies.
- **Surgical:** match existing entity/config/scene style; do not delete
  unrelated dead code (report it instead).
- **UK English** in all written output and documentation.
- **Gating:** implementation proceeds only through `/skill:implement`; this
  intake does not authorise code changes.

## Existing state (verified 2026-09-27 against HEAD)

- Enemy archetypes are **data, not code**: `EnemyConfig` (`src/core/configTypes.ts`),
  one CSV row per archetype (`src/data/enemy-configs.csv`), seed fallbacks in
  `src/core/configDefaults.ts`, factory mapping in `src/entities/enemyFactory.ts`.
- All regular enemies are **1 HP** (destroyed by a single bullet) and the GDD
  states this explicitly (`docs/Game Design Document.md` §2.3, §4.1, §6.5).
  Only the Boss is multi-hit (4-phase). There is an optional `takeDamage?()`
  seam on entities (`CombatCoreScene`, `CombatScene`, `GymFormationScene`), but
  the shared generic path currently calls it **without** running
  `onEnemyDestroyed()`/destruction audio when the entity finally dies — that
  is a gap this work must close for a multi-hit regular enemy to score, drop
  minerals and advance waves correctly.
- The Asteroid is the precedent for a **non-formation roamer**: it has
  `formationKind: single`, overrides `updatePosition(dt)` (called by the gym
  and game before `applyFormationPosition`) and `applyFormationPosition` is a
  no-op. Asteroids use the same random offscreen spawner
  (`src/waves/AsteroidSpawner.ts`) registered with the `WaveManager`.
- Minerals already exist: `Mineral` (`src/entities/Mineral.ts`), collection and
  non-asteroid absorption in `src/scenes/core/mineralLayer.ts`
  (`collectMinerals`), kill re-drop in `src/scenes/core/mineralKillDrops.ts`,
  and the 25–50 % re-drop fraction in `src/core/rules.ts`. `BaseEnemy` already
  tracks `mineralCount` / `collectMineral()` / `mineralRedropCount()`.
- The shared enemy-fire dispatcher (`src/entities/enemyFire.ts`) already
  mentions the "planned Harvester" as the example of a one-line wiring change.

## Desired change

1. Generalise enemy health data-driven: add a `health` CSV column + codec +
   `EnemyConfig.health` (default 1), and make the shared collision path
   correctly finalise a multi-hit kill (audio, `onEnemyDestroyed`, drops, wave
   accounting).
2. Add a `Harvester` entity (`health = 5`) that roams (like the Asteroid) and
   steers toward the nearest live mineral, absorbing it on overlap; no firing.
3. Register the archetype (CSV + seed + factory + score ≈ 400) and expose it in
   the gym.
4. Integrate it into the campaign as a rare roaming spawn in later levels,
   registered with the `WaveManager`.
5. Update the GDD/ENEMY design docs/README for the health-model and enemy
   catalog changes.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/data/enemy-configs.csv` — New `harvester` row (`health = 5`); add a
  `health` column to every row (default 1).
- `src/core/configTypes.ts` — `health` field on `EnemyConfig`.
- `src/core/csv.ts` — `health` column in `ENEMY_COLUMN_ORDER`, coercion and
  validation.
- `src/core/configDefaults.ts` — `harvester` seed fallback (+ default health 1
  for existing seeds).
- `src/entities/Harvester.ts` — New roamer entity: slow seek movement, large
  body, five-hit health, no firing.
- `src/entities/BaseEnemy.ts` — Shared multi-hit health / `takeDamage`
  behaviour (or a small shared health helper).
- `src/entities/enemyFactory.ts` — Map `harvester` → `Harvester`.
- `src/entities/enemyFire.ts` — No-firing archetype handling (the Harvester
  must not fall back to the aimed shot).
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` — Finalise a multi-hit kill through
  `onEnemyDestroyed` + destruction audio; supply the live mineral field to
  seeking entities.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — Wire seeking/minerals, score value, roamer
  movement, wave/score accounting.
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` + `src/scenes/gym/GymEnemies.ts` —
  Expose the same mineral list/seek seam and multi-hit path.
- `src/waves/Formations.ts` / `src/waves/AsteroidSpawner.ts` /
  `src/waves/sequencedLevels.ts` — Campaign roaming-spawn integration.
- `src/core/constants.ts` — `SCORE_VALUES.harvester` ≈ 400.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md`, `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`,
  `README.md` — Documentation updates.
- Tests: `src/entities/Harvester.test.ts`,
  `src/entities/enemyFactory.test.ts`, `src/core/csv.test.ts`,
  `src/core/enemyConfig.test.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymEnemies.test.ts`,
  `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`,
  `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`.

## Related work

- `AH-0MUII2FJ5007MDDA` — Gym↔game behavioural-parity epic (critical, open).
  This work must consume the shared cores it establishes and must not add a new
  divergence.
- `AH-0MUII3BBW000XZ46` — Shared enemy-fire dispatch (completed). Names the
  Harvester as the exemplar of one-line fire wiring.
- `AH-0MUII3DHM008L7JF` — Shared mineral layer: collection, hold/overflow,
  choice overlay (completed).
- `AH-0MUHMT5JC004WRSB` — Gym asteroids do not drop minerals / shared
  kill-drop rule (open); relevant to the re-drop path.
- `AH-0MU8BZ2ZM004J47F` — E6 Asteroid non-formation roamer (completed).
  Precedent architecture for a roaming enemy.
- `AH-0MT7V5UH90023XWR` — Clarify enemy health / one-hit destruction model in
  GDD (completed). The GDD's 1-HP rule is revised by this work (see Resolved
  decisions).
- `AH-0MTZWZ7MC002B01K` — Enemy difficulty scoring (completed). Health is not
  currently a scored factor.
- `AH-0MUJPTR7Q0070BDT` — Add a health factor to the enemy difficulty index
  (created, low priority, `discovered-from:AH-0MUI820PM0038HS2`). Tracks the
  difficulty-scoring follow-up so it does not creep into this item.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk — multi-hit kill does not finalise.** The current
  `onPlayerBulletHitsEnemy` `takeDamage` branch skips `onEnemyDestroyed` and
  destruction audio. Mitigation: extend the shared seam and pin it with a test
  so score/wave/drop/audio happen exactly once on the killing blow.
- **Risk — seek seam duplication.** Giving the entity the mineral list must be
  done once in the shared collision/tick path, not copied into each scene
  (parity epic). Mitigation: add a single `setSeekTargets`/equivalent seam
  alongside the existing `setAimTarget`.
- **Risk — health-model regression.** Generalising health could accidentally
  weaken the one-hit guarantee for existing enemies. Mitigation: `health`
  defaults to 1 and a regression test asserts one-hit destruction for every
  existing archetype.
- **Risk — difficulty under-scoring.** `enemyDifficulty` has no health factor.
  Mitigation: tracked separately as `AH-0MUJPTR7Q0070BDT`.
- **Risk — scope creep into wave/level design.** Wiring a new roamer into the
  campaign can balloon. Mitigation: scope is a rare roaming spawn in Levels 4–5
  only; the gym demonstration is the tuning surface.
- **Assumption — "collects it" reuses existing absorption.** The Harvester
  absorbs the mineral on overlap and tallies it; on death it re-drops 25–50 %
  per the existing rule.
- **Assumption — no dedicated health bar.** Feedback for non-lethal hits is the
  existing bullet-impact VFX (plus bullet consumption) rather than a drawn
  health bar; the producer's Q1 sub-question was not separately answered, so
  this minimal readable feedback is the default and can be revisited.
- **Assumption — tuning values are implementation/gym choices.** "Large" and
  "slow" are the requirements; exact px size/speed/colour are chosen and tuned
  in the gym (indicative: size ≈ 40–48 px, speed ≈ 20–30 px/s).
- **Assumption — the Harvester does not fire.**

## Resolved decisions (producer, 2026-09-27)

1. **Health model — data-driven.** Add a `health` column to the enemy-config
   pipeline and generalise multi-hit destruction for regular enemies; update the
   GDD. P4 Bomb continues to deal no damage to enemies. No dedicated health bar
   (minimal impact feedback); see Assumptions.
2. **Mineral-seeking semantics — literal seek.** Always seek the nearest live
   mineral anywhere on the field; absorb on overlap; no firing; cannot steal
   from the player's hold; existing 25–50 % re-drop applies.
3. **Spawn / campaign integration — gym + rare campaign roamer.** Available in
   the gym and added as a rare roaming spawn in later levels.
4. **Score / difficulty — score ≈ 400; difficulty health factor deferred.** The
   `enemyDifficulty` health factor is a separate follow-up
   (`AH-0MUJPTR7Q0070BDT`).

## Appendix — clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 (blocking) — Health model.** "A five-hit regular enemy contradicts the
  GDD's explicit 1-HP model. Options: (a) generalise health data-driven (new
  `health` CSV column + config type/codec + GDD update; P4 Bomb still deals no
  damage); (b) Harvester-only code constant; (c) other. Sub-question: should
  each non-lethal hit show a health indicator, or is ordinary hit feedback
  enough?" — **Answer (operator, interactive reply): "1. a".** Decision:
  data-driven `health` column + GDD update; P4 unchanged. Sub-question left to
  the minimal-feedback assumption above.
- **Q2 (blocking) — Mineral-seeking semantics.** "Options: (a) always seek the
  nearest live mineral anywhere on the field; absorb on overlap; no firing;
  cannot steal from the player's hold; re-drop 25–50 % per the existing rule;
  (b) only within a detection radius; (c) also fire at the player." — **Answer
  (operator, interactive reply): "2. a".**
- **Q3 (blocking) — Spawn / campaign integration.** "Options: (a) available in
  the gym and added to the campaign as a rare roaming spawn in later levels;
  (b) gym-only for now; (c) a fixed formation group." — **Answer (operator,
  interactive reply): "3. a".**
- **Q4 (non-blocking) — Score and difficulty weight.** "Recommended: score
  ≈ 400 (durable, between Tank 300 and Boss phases) and a linked follow-up to
  add a `health` factor to `enemyDifficulty`." — **Answer (operator,
  interactive reply): "4. a".** Follow-up item created:
  `AH-0MUJPTR7Q0070BDT`.
- Q (self-directed, repo research): "Is the Harvester already tracked or
  referenced?" — Research: `wl search harvester` and repo grep. Result: only
  this item and a code comment in `src/entities/enemyFire.ts` naming the
  "planned Harvester"; `src/entities/enemyFire.test.ts` uses `'harvester'` as
  a fallback-key example. No duplicate work item exists.
- Q (self-directed, repo research): "Does multi-hit support already exist for
  regular enemies?" — Research: inspected `CombatScene.onPlayerBulletHitsEnemy`,
  `GymFormationScene` `FormationSceneEntity.takeDamage`, and `Boss.takeDamage`.
  Result: an optional `takeDamage` seam exists, but the shared generic path
  does not finalise a kill (`onEnemyDestroyed`/destruction audio) — a gap to
  close (see Risks).
- Q (self-directed, repo research): "How do minerals and roaming enemies
  currently work?" — Research: read `mineralLayer.ts`, `Mineral.ts`,
  `mineralKillDrops.ts`, `BaseEnemy` mineral accounting, `Asteroid.ts` and
  `AsteroidSpawner.ts`. Result: absorption + re-drop and the non-formation
  roamer/spawner patterns both exist and are reusable; the only new capability
  is *seeking* the nearest mineral.

# Test: shared mineral kill-drop rule

Test-first task for AH-0MUHMT5JC004WRSB (AC3, AC5).

## Goal

Write deterministic unit + guard tests that pin the contract of the shared mineral kill-drop rule **before** it is implemented, so `PlayScene` and the gyms provably share one rule.

## Required coverage

- Small asteroid (`getSizeTier() === 'small'`) → exactly one mineral drop at the asteroid's death position.
- Large and medium asteroid → no direct drop (their small split children drop).
- Non-asteroid enemy that absorbed N minerals → re-drops between `mineralRedropFractionMin` and `mineralRedropFractionMax` of N, never more than N, at the death site, using a seeded RNG for determinism.
- Non-asteroid enemy with 0 absorbed minerals → no drops.
- Re-drop scatter stays within `MINERAL_REDROP_SCATTER_RADIUS` of the death site.

## Assumption

Shared helper module path: `src/scenes/core/mineralKillDrops.ts` exporting `resolveMineralKillDrops(scene, entity, rng): Mineral[]` (operator selected the shared-helper approach — see the parent item's Appendix).

# Phase Shift — auto-apply when the player is in danger

## Problem statement

Phase Shift (P6) currently grants a fixed 3 s of intangibility when collected (or permanently when chosen from the hold-full reward), which does not fit the game's moment-to-moment play: the player has to anticipate danger and activate at the right time, and the reward is frequently wasted. We want Phase Shift to become an **automatic, reactive defensive tool** that fires the instant the player is in real danger, lasts long enough to escape (1.5 s), and is unmistakably communicated through audio-visual "juice". A permanently-bought Phase Shift grants unlimited uses; a normally-collected one grants a finite number of uses.

## Users

- **Player (primary):** "As a player, when I am about to be overwhelmed by enemies or bullets, I want my Phase Shift to trigger automatically so I can escape without having to track a timer or press a key, and I want the screen to clearly tell me I am intangible."
- **Player (permanent purchase):** "As a player who chose Phase Shift from the hold-full reward, I want unlimited automatic phase shifts for the rest of the run so the reward feels genuinely powerful."
- **Developer / maintainer:** "As a developer, I want the danger-detection and auto-trigger logic to live in the shared power-up layer so the shipped game and every combat gym behave identically (no divergent copies)."

## Existing state

- `src/powerups/effects.ts` — `EffectsRegistry` owns P6 as a timed effect (`P6_PHASE_DURATION = 3`); `applyPhaseShift()` activates/refreshes it (used by P7 teleport), `applyCollect('P6', permanent?)` starts it, `isPhased` / `isHitImmune` read it. `permanent` (hold-full choice) never expires.
- Collision gating already respects phase: `CombatScene.isPlayerPhased()` → `getEffectsRegistry().isPhased`; `_handleCollisions()` skips the enemy-bullet-vs-player and player-vs-enemy passes while phased. `PlayScene._handleAsteroidCollisions()` has an equivalent early return.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatEffectVisuals.ts` draws the shared P6 ghost (ship alpha `0.45`, blink-aware) via `applyPhaseGhost()`, used by `PlayScene`, `GymPowerUpsCombat` and `GymFormationScene`.
- `src/core/constants.ts` — `SHIP_SIZE = 20`, `PLAYER_BULLET_RADIUS = 3`, player hull = `SHIP_SIZE / 2`.
- Mineral collection lives in `src/scenes/core/mineralLayer.ts` and `PlayScene` (`_collectMineral` / `onPlayerCollected`); nothing currently blocks collection while phased.
- Juice precedent: `src/vfx/playerDeathJuice.ts` (camera shake + flash + particles, per-layer toggles) and `src/vfx/bulletImpact.ts`; procedural WebAudio cues live in `src/audio/effects.ts` (all safe no-ops without an AudioContext, so headless tests never break).
- No danger-detection / proximity-threat logic exists today.

## Desired change

1. **Danger detection** — each frame, count hostile threats whose centre lies within `DANGER_RADIUS = 2 × SHIP_SIZE` (40 px) of the ship: enemy bodies (including asteroids, boss and minions) plus live enemy bullets. When the combined count reaches `DANGER_THREAT_THRESHOLD = 3`, the player is "in danger".
2. **Auto-trigger (P6 charge)** — when in danger and a Phase Shift charge is available (or the run holds the permanent Phase Shift), automatically activate Phase Shift for `PHASE_DURATION = 1.5 s`. A normally-collected P6 grants a stored auto-activation charge; the permanent (hold-full) P6 grants unlimited activations.
3. **Pass-through / collection gate** — while phased, bullets and enemies pass straight through the player (already implemented) and the player **cannot collect minerals** (new gate).
4. **Juice** — screen-wide, unmistakable phase feedback: all on-screen enemies, bullets and minerals are visually distorted/faded/shaken (e.g. chromatic-aberration style split-tint or desaturation + shake), the ship keeps its ghost alpha, and a distinct sci-fi Phase Shift sound plays on every activation.
5. **P7 teleport unchanged in mechanic** — teleport still activates Phase Shift on arrival; only the duration becomes 1.5 s (assumption; see Open Questions).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Danger detection is measurable and correct.** A pure, unit-testable helper counts hostile entities + hostile bullets within `2 × SHIP_SIZE` of the ship and reports "in danger" when the combined count is ≥ 3. Boundary cases are covered: exactly 3 threats triggers; 2 threats do not; threats just inside the radius count and just outside do not; asteroids, boss/minions and all enemy bullet types count; player bullets and minerals do not.
- [ ] **AC2 — Auto-trigger semantics.** When in danger and a P6 activation is available, Phase Shift activates automatically for exactly 1.5 s without any player input, and the 1.5 s countdown replaces the old 3 s duration everywhere (drop, hold-full, P7 arrival). The re-arm rule after expiry is implemented per the producer answer to Q2 (danger must clear below threshold before re-arming, plus a ~0.5 s re-arm cooldown) and unit-tested for both the charge and permanent cases.
- [ ] **AC3 — Charges and permanence.** A normally-collected P6 grants a finite number of auto-activations (one per pickup, per the producer answer to Q3) that is decremented on trigger and visible in the HUD; a hold-full permanent P6 grants unlimited activations. Tests cover: charge consumed on trigger, no trigger with zero charges, permanent triggers repeatedly.
- [ ] **AC4 — Pass-through and mineral gate.** While phased, enemy bodies and bullets do not hit the player (existing behaviour retained, regression-tested) and mineral collection is blocked; mineral collection resumes immediately after expiry. Power-up / weapon drop collection behaviour is per Open Question Q7.
- [ ] **AC5 — Juice and audio.** On every Phase Shift activation, all on-screen enemies, bullets and minerals receive the shared phase visual treatment (fade/shake and/or global distortion) for the duration of the effect and it is cleanly cleared on expiry; the ship ghost remains. A dedicated sci-fi Phase Shift WebAudio cue plays on activation and degrades to a safe no-op without an AudioContext. The visual layers are toggleable (mirroring `playerDeathJuice`) and unit-tested for state transitions; audio presence is asserted via the existing audio-test seams.
- [ ] **AC6 — Testing/validation.** New automated unit/integration tests cover danger detection, auto-trigger timing, charge/permanent semantics, the mineral gate and visual/audio wiring, and they fail against the pre-change implementation (TDD where practical). Manual `npm run dev` check confirms the visual/audio feedback reads clearly in-game.
- [ ] **AC7 — Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, `README.md`, `docs/Game Design Document.md` (§4.4 P6/P7 entries) and `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` hit-gating notes. (`CHANGELOG.md` is managed by the release pipeline and is excluded.)
- [ ] **AC8 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- Engine-agnostic logic stays in `src/powerups` (no Phaser imports), mirroring the existing registry/test split; rendering and audio stay in scenes / `src/vfx` / `src/audio`.
- The single shared combat path must be preserved: `PlayScene`, `GymPowerUpsCombat` and `GymFormationScene` must all inherit the same auto-trigger behaviour (no per-scene copies) — enforced by the existing cross-scene equivalence tests.
- Audio must remain a safe no-op without an AudioContext (headless tests must not break).
- Exclude CI/CD pipeline tests and `CHANGELOG.md` from the ACs.
- Do not regress P7 teleport safety or the existing P3/P6 hit-gating.

## Desired change / behaviour summary

The player no longer manages Phase Shift actively. The ship "phases out" on its own the moment three or more threats close within two ship-widths, escapes through them for 1.5 s, and the whole screen visibly and audibly "shifts" to sell the effect. Collecting P6 stock-piles finite auto-uses; the hold-full reward makes them unlimited.

- `src/powerups/effects.ts` — Replace/extend P6 timed-effect model with charge + permanent auto-activation; expose danger trigger state, charge count per activation, and a hook the scene calls with "in danger".
- `src/powerups/dangerDetection.ts` (new) — Pure proximity/danger helper (threat count within radius), unit-tested.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` / `CombatCoreScene.ts` — Feed live enemy/bullet positions into the danger check each frame; own the auto-trigger call and the mineral-collection gate.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — Wire danger detection, mineral gate, and the new juice/sound on activation.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.ts`, `src/scenes/core/CombatEffectVisuals.ts` — Ensure the gym shares the same auto-trigger and visual treatment.
- `src/vfx/phaseShiftJuice.ts` (new) — Screen-wide phase visual treatment (fade/shake/distortion), layer toggles for tests.

- `docs/Game Design Document.md`, `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`, `README.md` — Documentation updates.

- **Scope-creep risk:** the juice work (chromatic aberration / screen distortion) can balloon. Keep it to one shared, toggleable module; record anything beyond the agreed aesthetic as a linked follow-up rather than expanding scope.
- **Balance risk:** if Phase Shift re-arms while still surrounded, a permanent P6 can make the player permanently invincible. The re-arm rule (Q2) is the key mitigation and must be decided before implementation.

- **Q1 — Danger-count semantics.** Does "3 or more enemies or bullets within 2× the ship's size" mean the *combined* count of enemy bodies + hostile bullets within the radius ≥ 3, or separate thresholds? — Answer (producer): **combined**. Accepted: the combined count of all hostile threats (enemy bodies incl. asteroids/boss/minions plus enemy bullets) whose centre is within 40 px (2 × `SHIP_SIZE`) of the ship, threshold ≥ 3. # Intake Brief — When ships explode when a level times out we need major SFX explosion (AH-0MUJ1YZJ9008O4RC)

## Headline

Add a new dedicated, layered "major explosion" SFX to the wave-timeout path,
played once per detonating ship (with a concurrency/rate limiter), so the 10×
detonation of surviving enemies is no longer silent.

## Problem statement

When a wave times out, every surviving non-asteroid enemy detonates at 10×
scale (`WAVE_TIMEOUT_EXPLOSION_SCALE`), but no explosion sound plays for those
detonations. The only audio on the timeout path is the generic player
life-loss cue (`playDestructionSound()` via `_loseLife(false)`), so the
dramatic 10× visual blast lands silently and the moment reads as flat.

## Users

- **Player** — the wave-timeout wipe should be audible as a major explosion,
  making the lost life and the 10× detonation feel consequential.
- **Developer / designer tuning feel** — one place (exported constants) to tune
  the cue's layering, volume, duration and voice cap.

### Example user story

- As a **player**, when the level timer hits zero and my remaining enemies
  detonate, I hear a large, heavy explosion cue so the moment reads as a major
  event rather than a silent animation.

## Existing state

- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — `_timeoutWave()` detonates every non-asteroid
  survivor via `s.entity.destroySelf(WAVE_TIMEOUT_EXPLOSION_SCALE)` and calls
  `_loseLife(false)`; it plays **no SFX for the detonations**.
  `WAVE_TIMEOUT_EXPLOSION_SCALE = 10`.
- `src/entities/BaseEnemy.ts` — `destroySelf(scale)` → `playExplosion(scale)`
  only spawns particles; the class comment states audio is played by the scene
  at destruction time.
- `src/audio/effects.ts` — `playDestructionSound()` (generic 440→60 Hz
  sawtooth pop) and the layered `playPlayerDestructionSound()` (impact thump +
  descending body + noise tail). No "major" or timeout-specific cue exists.
- GDD §7.3 documents the two existing cues and states "the wave-timeout life
  penalty and shield absorption keep the generic cue". It also flags the risk
  "SFX rate limiting — … avoid stacking more than 3–4 concurrent SFX
  instances".
- Tests live in `src/audio/effects.test.ts`, `src/audio/effectsMaster.test.ts`
  and `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`.

## Desired change

Add a new dedicated, layered `playMajorExplosionSound()` cue in
`src/audio/effects.ts` and wire it into `PlayScene._timeoutWave()` so it fires
once per detonating ship, guarded by a concurrency/rate limiter so stacked cues
stay within the GDD §7.3 audio ceiling. Document the new cue in GDD §7.3 and
cover it with automated tests.

## Producer decisions (recorded)

- **Q1 — Blast granularity: B** → one heavy cue **per detonating ship**, with
  attenuation/rate-limiting.
- **Q2 — Cue identity: A** → a **new dedicated** `playMajorExplosionSound()`,
  not a reuse of `playPlayerDestructionSound()`.
- **Q3 — Player life-loss cue on timeout: A** → keep the **generic**
  `playDestructionSound()` for the player's timeout life loss; only the enemy
  detonations get the major blast cue.

## Assumptions

1. The limiter caps concurrent major-explosion voices at an exported
   `MAJOR_EXPLOSION_MAX_VOICES` (default aligned to the GDD's "≤ 3–4 concurrent
   SFX" guidance); triggers beyond the cap are coalesced/attenuated rather than
   stacking at full gain. [ASSUMPTION]
2. Scope is audio only — the 10× particle blast already exists, so no new VFX.
   [ASSUMPTION]
3. `PlayScene` is the only wave-timeout path (no gym scene has a wave timeout),
   so wiring is confined to `PlayScene._timeoutWave()`. [ASSUMPTION]
4. The cue routes through the existing SFX master gain/mute plumbing and is a
   safe no-op without an `AudioContext` (headless tests, autoplay-blocked
   browsers). [ASSUMPTION]

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A new dedicated `playMajorExplosionSound()` is defined in
   `src/audio/effects.ts` using layered procedural synthesis (impact thump +
   descending body + noise tail), with every amplitude, duration and voice-cap
   value exposed as an exported `MAJOR_EXPLOSION_*` constant; the cue is
   documented in GDD §7.3.
2. When a wave/level times out with surviving non-asteroid enemies, the major
   explosion cue is triggered **once per detonating ship** (verified by a
   `PlayScene` test whose spy count equals the number of detonated survivors).
3. A concurrency/rate limiter keeps stacked per-ship cues within the GDD §7.3
   audio ceiling: no more than `MAJOR_EXPLOSION_MAX_VOICES` concurrent
   major-explosion voices, with excess triggers attenuated/coalesced — verified
   by unit tests that exercise many simultaneous triggers.
4. When a wave/level times out with no enemies remaining, no major-explosion
   cue plays and the player's generic life-loss cue is unchanged (no
   `playPlayerDestructionSound()` on this path) — verified by tests.
5. The cue routes through the SFX master volume/mute and is a safe no-op
   without an `AudioContext` — verified by tests.
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- All SFX remain **procedural** (Web Audio API, zero external audio assets) per
  GDD §7.3.
- Respect the GDD §7.3 ceiling and the "avoid stacking more than 3–4 concurrent
  SFX instances" risk mitigation.
- No new gameplay behaviour: the timeout detonation/one-life penalty is
  unchanged; this is feedback only.
- No new VFX.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/audio/effects.ts` — Add `playMajorExplosionSound()` and its
  `MAJOR_EXPLOSION_*` tuning/limiter constants (mirroring the layered
  `playPlayerDestructionSound()` structure).
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — Call the new cue once per detonating ship in
  `_timeoutWave()` (alongside `destroySelf(WAVE_TIMEOUT_EXPLOSION_SCALE)`);
  leave `_loseLife(false)` and its generic cue untouched.
- `src/audio/effects.test.ts` / `src/audio/effectsMaster.test.ts` — Unit tests
  for layering, limiter/voice cap, master volume/mute routing and
  no-AudioContext no-op.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` — Timeout wiring tests (one cue per ship, none
  when no enemies, generic player cue unchanged).
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §7.3 SFX event catalog and player audio
  character section: document the new major-explosion cue and its limiter.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Limiter tuning may need an audio playtest.** Whether the per-ship stack
  reads as one "major" blast or as mud cannot be judged from unit tests alone;
  `MAJOR_EXPLOSION_MAX_VOICES` and per-voice gain are exported for tuning.
  [Medium]
- **Masking/clipping risk.** Many near-simultaneous heavy cues could mask
  other SFX or clip; mitigated by the voice cap/attenuation (GDD §7.3 "avoid
  stacking more than 3–4 concurrent SFX instances"). [Medium]
- **Browser autoplay policy.** The cue stays silent until a user gesture
  starts the `AudioContext`; it must remain a safe no-op when no context
  exists. [Low]
- **Scope-creep guard.** Reusing the new major cue for other events (boss
  death, P4 bomb clear, player death) is out of scope; record those as linked
  work items rather than widening this item. [Low]
- **Assumption:** no gym wave-timeout path exists today; if one is added
  later, it must reuse the same cue + limiter rather than duplicating it.
  [Low]

## Related work

- AH-0MU7JTG9R002ZWA6 — Wave time limit: surviving enemies detonate at 10x
  scale and cost a life (added the timeout detonation; completed).
- AH-0MU8TWF1H007OG2L — Asteroids should not explode when time runs out,
  instead carry them over (completed).
- AH-0MUAYB4R3002ZIZY — Need juice when the player is destroyed (precedent for
  a dedicated layered cue; completed).
- AH-0MUDY2ID7006VY3A — dedicated player-destruction cue (implemented
  `playPlayerDestructionSound`).
- AH-0MTV6ADT4001FB2V — Add particle-based explosion VFX for enemy and player
  deaths (completed).
- AH-0MU0AVBWH002ZWRH — Add randomness to explosion (completed).
- AH-0MUA8B6MT006M1KS — SFX master volume + mute plumbing in effects.ts
  (completed).
- AH-0MUA8BEUR006RWCI — SettingsScene: SFX volume slider + mute toggle
  (completed).
- AH-0MU3VPIA900697E8 — Ensure all enemies have SFX on their fire event
  (completed).
- AH-0MT7UW0Y80062NU1 — Bring simple audio effects into MVP scope in GDD
  (completed).

## Related work (automated report)

> Generated by the `find-related` skill. Conservative ranking; treat as
> suggestions, not a complete list.

### Related work items
- **AH-0MUBYXR280018HST** – PlayScene: wire absorb animation + pop SFX into collection path (completed)
- **AH-0MTFU1GAO009KDBM** – [test-failure] <suite exited 1>: npm --silent test — failing test (completed)
- **AH-0MU4KQ6NT006MP52** – Extract common enemy base class for regular enemies (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: absorption, ac3, acceptance, add, added (+200 more)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: absorption, ac3, add, added, also (+199 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: add, added, already, also, animation (+160 more)

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — Blast granularity: Should the "major SFX explosion" be one cue per
  timeout event, or one cue per detonating ship?** — Answer (producer, via
  interactive reply): **B) one heavy cue per detonating ship, with
  attenuation/rate-limiting.** Agent recommendation had been A (single cue);
  producer chose B, so a limiter is now an explicit AC. Final accepted answer:
  B.
- **Q2 — Cue identity: Should this be a new dedicated cue or a reuse of an
  existing one?** — Answer (producer, via interactive reply): **A) a new
  dedicated `playMajorExplosionSound()`.** Final accepted answer: A.
- **Q3 — Player life-loss cue on timeout: upgrade to the heavy
  player-destruction cue, or only the enemy detonations?** — Answer (producer,
  via interactive reply): **A) keep the generic player life-loss cue and add
  only the blast cue.** Final accepted answer: A.

# Single-formation wave groups can declare more enemies than they spawn

## Problem statement

`WaveManager.waveEnemyCount()` (`_waveSize`) reports a wave's declared size by
summing each group's `count`, but `planGroupSpawns` builds the actual spawn list
from the group's formation builder — and `buildSingleOffset`
(`src/utils/formations.ts`) deliberately ignores its `count` argument and always
returns exactly one offset. A `single`-formation group with `count > 1`
therefore declares more enemies than it spawns, so the alive count seeded by
`beginGame()` (`_waveSize(currentWave())`) exceeds `planSpawns().length`. The
wave-clear invariant (`enemiesAlive` reaches zero only after every planned spawn
is destroyed) then relies on the player destroying enemies that were never
spawned, and any future sequencer/authoring path that emits `count > 1` for a
`single` group can stall or clear a wave early.

## Users

- **Level designer / content author** — hand-authors or retunes level/wave
  definitions (and may later widen sequencer count ranges); needs a wave's
  declared enemy count to match what actually spawns, or an immediate,
  actionable validation error when it cannot.
- **Player** — experiences correct wave pacing: a wave must not stall waiting on
  enemies that never spawned, nor clear while spawned enemies remain.
- **Reviewer / producer** — needs the "declared == planned" invariant pinned by
  a regression test, and the resolution direction (validate vs. account from
  planned spawns) recorded so it stays auditable.

Example user stories:

- *As a level designer, I want a wave's declared enemy count to equal its
  planned spawns, so that wave-clear accounting cannot diverge from what the
  player faces.*
- *As a level designer, I want a clear validation error if I configure a
  `single`-formation group with `count > 1`, so that I can correct the data
  rather than debug a stalled wave.*
- *As a reviewer, I want a regression test pinning the declared-vs-planned
  invariant for the `single` formation, so that the defect cannot silently
  return.*

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Declared count matches planned spawns (or is rejected).** For any wave
  containing a `single`-formation group, either
  `waveEnemyCount() === planSpawns().length`, or the wave is rejected with a
  clear validation error/message that names the offending group and its
  `count`. The inconsistent state (declared > planned) must not be reachable.
- **AC2 — Regression test pins the invariant.** A unit test asserts the
  declared-vs-planned invariant for a `single`-formation group, including the
  `count > 1` case (either equal counts, or a thrown/returned validation error
  with the expected message). Existing `single` semantics
  (`buildSingleOffset` always returns one centred offset) remain pinned.
- **AC3 — No regression in the built-in campaign or sequencer calibration.**
  `src/waves/WaveManager.test.ts`, `src/waves/sequencedLevels.test.ts`,
  `src/core/difficultySequencer.test.ts` and
  `src/waves/enemyDifficulty.campaign.test.ts` remain green; any test that
  currently relies on an inconsistent `single` group (e.g. `wave('asteroid',
  'single', 2)`) is updated to a valid configuration rather than left asserting
  the broken behaviour.
- **AC4 — Documentation updated.** In-code comments on `buildSingleOffset` /
  `planGroupSpawns` / `_waveSize` (and the chosen validation/accounting helper)
  state that a `single` group represents exactly one entity and that declared
  and planned counts must agree. `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` is
  updated where it describes formation kinds/geometry and wave groups. All
  related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
  comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- **AC5 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- **Do not change `buildSingleOffset`'s single-entity semantics.** It is
  documented as "Single-entity formation for the Boss" and pinned by
  `src/utils/formations.test.ts` (`buildSingleOffset(99)` and
  `buildSingleOffset(0)` both return `[{ row: 0, col: 0 }]`). The `single`
  formation means one entity; making it emit `count` overlapping offsets would
  contradict the type name, the Boss usage and the existing test.
- **One code path (gym↔game parity).** Formation geometry and wave spawn
  planning stay in the shared core (`src/utils/formations.ts`,
  `src/waves/WaveManager.ts`); no divergent copy in gyms or scenes
  (AGENTS.md "Gym↔game parity").
- **Pure and deterministic.** Wave planning/validation must remain free of
  Phaser runtime dependencies so it stays unit-testable
  (`planGroupSpawns` is pure; `WaveManager` is a pure state machine).
- **Preserve the sequencer guard.** The `defaultCandidatePool()` guard added in
  AH-0MUDYTPMC002GLEJ (pinning `single`-formation archetypes to their seed
  count, `src/core/difficultySequencer.ts`) remains; this item fixes the
  underlying inconsistency, it does not remove the guard.
- **UK English** in all docs and comments.
- **Scope discipline:** changing gym-scene enemy configurator `count`
  behaviour, or `buildSingleOffset` semantics, is out of scope; record any
  additional opportunities as linked follow-ups rather than folding them in.

## Existing state

- `src/waves/WaveManager.ts`
  - `_waveSize(wave)` (≈ line 240) sums `group.count` across groups.
  - `waveEnemyCount()` (≈ line 246) returns `_waveSize(currentWave())`.
  - `planSpawns()` (≈ line 256) delegates to `planGroupSpawns(wave.groups, …)`.
  - `planGroupSpawns(groups, shootEnabled)` (≈ line 359) iterates
    `buildOffsets(groupDef.count)` and emits one `EnemySpawn` per returned
    offset.
  - `beginGame()` seeds `_enemiesAlive = _waveSize(currentWave())`.
- `src/utils/formations.ts`
  - `buildSingleOffset(_count)` (≈ line 153) returns `[{ row: 0, col: 0 }]`
    regardless of `count`.
  - `FORMATION_BUILDERS` / `getFormationBuilder` (≈ lines 161–172) map
    `'single'` to `buildSingleOffset`.
  - `EnemyFormationKind` includes `'single'` (also mirrored in
    `src/core/configTypes.ts:22` and `src/core/csv.ts:28`).
- `src/waves/Formations.ts` — `WaveGroup.count` is documented as "Number of
  enemies in this group"; the `group()` helper (≈ line 73) sets it from the
  author's literal. Built-in `LEVELS` use `'single'` only for the retired
  asteroid placement (now spawned dynamically) and the Boss with `count: 1`.
- `src/core/difficultySequencer.ts` — `defaultCandidatePool()` (≈ line 137)
  pins `single`-formation archetypes to their seed count; comment explicitly
  cites `buildSingleOffset` ignoring its argument. Regression test at
  `src/core/difficultySequencer.test.ts:321`.
- Tests that currently exercise inconsistent `single` groups:
  - `src/waves/WaveManager.test.ts:411` and `:419` build
    `wave('asteroid', 'single', 2)`; `:419` asserts `enemiesAlive` is `2`.
  - `src/utils/formations.test.ts:29–30,41–43` pin `buildSingleOffset` to one
    offset regardless of `count`.
- No existing wave/level validation helper exists (no `validate*` in
  `src/waves/`). `Formations.ts` exposes `getLevelDefinition` /
  `enemyCountForLevel` (≈ lines 176–185) but no group-count validation.

## Desired change

1. Make the declared size and the planned spawn list agree for `single`
   groups. Recommended approach (see Risks & assumptions): keep
   `buildSingleOffset` single-entity, and make `_waveSize` /
   `waveEnemyCount()` derive from the planned spawns (or clamp `single` groups
   to one) so `waveEnemyCount() === planSpawns().length` for every wave.
2. Additionally, add a small pure validation helper (e.g.
   `validateWaveGroups` / `validateLevelDefinitions` in
   `src/waves/WaveManager.ts` or `src/waves/Formations.ts`) that reports a
   clear error naming the offending group and `count` when a `single`-
   formation group has `count !== 1`. Decide — and document — whether this is
   a hard reject (thrown at plan/validation time) or a clamp; the AC accepts
   either, provided the inconsistent state cannot be observed.
3. Update the two `wave('asteroid', 'single', 2)` constructions in
   `WaveManager.test.ts` to a valid configuration (e.g. `count: 1`, adjusting
   the `enemiesAlive` expectation), and add the AC2 regression test.
4. Update the relevant doc/comment references (AC4).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/waves/WaveManager.ts` — `_waveSize` / `waveEnemyCount()` / `planSpawns`
  and (optionally) a new pure validation helper; doc comments stating the
  declared==planned invariant and `single` semantics.
- `src/utils/formations.ts` — document `buildSingleOffset` as one-entity (no
  behaviour change unless the validation approach requires a shared predicate
  here). Keep `formations.test.ts` green.
- `src/waves/WaveManager.test.ts` — fix the `single, 2` fixtures; add the AC2
  regression test pinning declared==planned (and/or the validation error).
- `src/waves/Formations.ts` — possibly home to a shared wave/level validation
  helper if placed with the data shapes; keep `LEVELS` valid.
- `src/core/difficultySequencer.ts` — likely no change (guard retained);
  confirm the comment still reflects the resolution.
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — formation-kind / wave-group
  documentation of the `single` == one-entity rule and declared==planned
  invariant.

## Related work

- **Add bullet TTL to enemy configurator (AH-0MUDYTPMC002GLEJ)** — parent
  discovery context; added the `defaultCandidatePool()` `single`-formation
  guard and its regression test (`difficultySequencer.test.ts:321`).
- **Implement runtime auto-sequencer for dynamic difficulty adjustment
  (AH-0MUDIWETP003XC3X)** — owns `src/core/difficultySequencer.ts`; may emit
  groups whose `count` must satisfy wave planning.
- **Campaign builder: config to generated level definitions
  (AH-0MUITS0VD000DVSV)** — maps `AdjustedGroup` → `WaveGroup`; the guard's
  guarantee flows through this path.
- **End-to-end acceptance tests for sequenced wave generation
  (AH-0MUITRWLO001Y4Y5)** — how sequencer output becomes playable waves.
- **Remove fixed asteroid group from Formations.ts (AH-0MUGCQ8MS000815U)** —
  explains why built-in `single` groups are now Boss-only (asteroids spawned
  dynamically via `AsteroidSpawner`).
- **Asteroids spawn randomly offscreen (AH-0MUDYS2SZ004H123)** — dynamic
  asteroid spawning (not a `single` formation group).
- **AsteroidSpawner (AH-0MUGCH1L0005HXDG)** and dynamic-spawn registration
  (**AH-0MU8BZ2ZM004J47F**, pinned by the `registerDynamicSpawn` tests in
  `WaveManager.test.ts`) — the split/registration path that makes declared vs
  planned counts safety-critical.
- **Filter asteroids in `_timeoutWave()` and re-register them (Phase 1)
  (AH-0MU97HEFA003YMVS)** — wave-timeout path that re-registers dynamic spawns,
  another consumer of the alive-count invariant.
- **Increase the possible number of enemies in a enemy formation to 200
  (AH-0MTV8Q1LV001KOA5)** — count-range precedent.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption (resolution direction).** The fix keeps `buildSingleOffset`
  single-entity and makes accounting/validation reject or normalise
  `single` groups with `count !== 1`, rather than making the builder honour
  `count`. Rationale: the builder is named/documented as single-entity, is
  used by the Boss, and is pinned by `formations.test.ts`. **Producer may
  confirm or redirect**; the AC accepts either equal counts or rejection.
- **Assumption (reject vs clamp).** Preferred: a clear validation error
  (fail fast, surfaces misconfiguration) rather than a silent clamp.
  **Producer may adjust**; either satisfies AC1.
- **Risk (existing tests encode the bug).** `WaveManager.test.ts:411/419`
  construct `single, count 2` and `:419` asserts `enemiesAlive === 2`.
  Mitigation: update these fixtures to a valid configuration and add the AC2
  regression test; do not preserve the broken expectation.
- **Risk (behaviour change to `enemiesAlive`).** Deriving `waveEnemyCount`
  from planned spawns changes the initial alive count for any inconsistent
  group. Mitigation: keep it equal to `planSpawns().length`, which is the
  source of truth for spawned entities; verify campaign/sequencer tests.
- **Risk (validation placed too eagerly).** Throwing during construction could
  break tests that only exercise dynamic-spawn accounting. Mitigation: choose
  and document the validation call site (plan/validation time) and cover it
  in the regression test.
- **Scope-creep risk:** changing gym-scene `count` handling or the CSV
  configurator is a separate concern; record as linked follow-up if raised.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MU97HEFA003YMVS** – Filter asteroids in _timeoutWave() and re-register them (Phase 1) (completed)
- **AH-0MU8BZ2ZM004J47F** – Asteroids as an enemy (completed)
- **AH-0MUAYB2L2002W7VC** – Boss is destroyed in one hit (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: acceptance, accounting, actually, add, adding (+72 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: accounting, actually, add, adding, always (+66 more)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: accounting, add, adding, always, applied (+63 more)

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No clarifying questions were asked: the seed context plus repository evidence
 (`src/waves/WaveManager.ts`, `src/utils/formations.ts`,
 `src/utils/formations.test.ts`, `src/core/difficultySequencer.ts`) were
sufficient to draft the brief. Decisions that would normally be interviewed are
recorded as explicit assumptions above:

- Q: "Should `buildSingleOffset(count)` honour `count`, or should wave
  accounting/validation be fixed instead?" — Answer: fix accounting/validation;
  keep the builder single-entity. Source: repo inspection —
  `buildSingleOffset` documented "Single-entity formation for the Boss"
  (`src/utils/formations.ts:152`), used by the Boss, and pinned by
  `src/utils/formations.test.ts:41–43` (`buildSingleOffset(99)` → one offset).
  (ASSUMPTION — producer confirmation welcome.)
- Q: "Should an offending `single` group be rejected or clamped?" — Answer:
  prefer a clear validation error; a clamp is acceptable per AC1.
  (ASSUMPTION — producer confirmation welcome.)
- Q: "Are the two `wave('asteroid', 'single', 2)` tests intentional?" —
  Answer: no; they encode the defect and should be updated. Source: this
  work item's problem statement and `formations.test.ts`.

# Intake Brief: Asteroids do not need to be cleared for a wave to be completed — AH-0MUJM746P000QAEO

**Priority: High** | **Type: bug** | **Assignee: Map**

> A wave must complete as soon as every non-asteroid (enemy ship) in it is
> destroyed. Asteroids no longer count toward a wave's alive target, and both
> asteroids and minerals persist in place across wave and level transitions.

## Problem Statement

Asteroids are currently registered with the `WaveManager` as dynamic spawns
(`registerDynamicSpawn(1)`) when they are released from the offscreen spawner
and when a large/medium asteroid splits. They therefore inflate the wave's
`enemiesAlive` counter, so a wave cannot complete until **every asteroid —
including every split child — is destroyed** (or the wave timer expires). This
forces players to chase slow, non-firing rocks to advance, and it contradicts
the intended rule that only enemy ships gate wave completion. It also causes
asteroids to be cleared/short-circuited at wave boundaries instead of behaving
like classic-Asteroids debris that lingers in the field.

## Users

- **Player (primary):** completes a wave by destroying the enemy ships, without
  having to sweep the field of drifting asteroids first.
  - *"As a player, I want a wave to complete as soon as the enemy ships are
    gone, so drifting asteroids don't stall my progress through the campaign."*
  - *"As a player, I want asteroids and minerals to persist between waves and
    levels, so the field feels like a continuous classic-Asteroids environment
    rather than resetting every wave."*
- **Developer / maintainer:** the wave-completion rule is expressed in one
  place (`WaveManager` accounting + how `PlayScene` feeds it), so it cannot
  drift between the game and its tests.
- **Tester:** can assert deterministic wave completion with live asteroids
  present, and asteroid/mineral persistence across transitions.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Wave completion ignores asteroids.** When all non-asteroid enemies in the
   active wave are destroyed, `WaveManager.onEnemyDestroyed()` returns
   `waveCleared` / `levelCleared` / `bossTriggered` as appropriate **regardless
   of how many asteroids (any tier) remain alive**. Asteroids and asteroid
   split children never increment `WaveManager.enemiesAlive`.
- **Asteroids persist.** Surviving asteroids remain alive in the scene across
   wave and level transitions, continuing straight-line motion, four-edge
   wrapping, rotation, and remaining shootable (player bullets still destroy
   them and still cascade splits).
- **Split behaviour preserved (gameplay only).** Destroying a large/medium
   asteroid still spawns exactly two smaller children at its position with
   divergent directions, and the children persist and can be shot; the split no
   longer affects wave accounting (no `registerDynamicSpawn`).
- **Wave-timeout unchanged for ships.** On wave-timeout, every surviving
   non-asteroid enemy still detonates at 10× scale and costs exactly one life;
   surviving asteroids are **not** re-registered with the `WaveManager` (they no
   longer gate the next wave) and remain alive and persistent.
- **Minerals persist.** Minerals already on the field remain in place across
   wave and level transitions and remain collectable (player) / absorbable
   (non-asteroid enemies); no new mineral behaviour is introduced.
- **Boss entry keeps clearing asteroids.** Carried-over asteroids are still
   destroyed when the boss encounter begins (the boss encounter spawns no
   asteroids). This preserves the documented boss-entry behaviour and is
   recorded as an assumption below.
- **Tests updated and comprehensive.** Unit/integration tests cover: wave
   clears with live asteroids present; `enemiesAlive` excludes asteroids and
   split children; asteroids persist across a wave and a level transition;
   timeout does not re-register asteroids. The existing contradictory tests
   (e.g. `AC6 — the wave clears only after ALL split children are destroyed`
   and `AH-0MU8TWF1H007OG2L AC5 — carried-over asteroids are re-registered…`)
   are replaced with tests for the new rule.
- **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including
   code comments, the GDD (§4.1 E6 "Wave placement" and §4.2 wave definition)
   and `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`.
- **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Scope is the game's wave model.** Only `PlayScene` + `WaveManager` own
  wave completion; the formation gyms (`src/scenes/gym/`) have no `WaveManager`
  and their wipe→respawn cycle is a training construct, so they are out of
  scope. The shared asteroid-split helper (`scenes/core/asteroidSplit.ts`) is
  unchanged, so game/gym split behaviour stays identical.
- **Gym↔game parity (AGENTS.md).** The split helper and mineral rules stay
  shared; only the wave-accounting call site in `PlayScene` changes. Document
  the reason for the `WaveManager`-only scope in the work item/comment.
- **Do not remove `registerDynamicSpawn` / `unregisterDynamicSpawn`** even if
  they become unused by asteroids; keep them as a general dynamic-spawn seam
  (mention as potentially unused rather than deleting).
- **No new spawner/balance tuning** (spawn cadence, tier weights, asteroid
  count) — those are out of scope.
- **Deterministic tests** only; no wall-clock waits.

## Existing State

- `WaveManager` (`src/waves/WaveManager.ts`) tracks `_enemiesAlive`, seeded from
  the wave's formation groups. `onEnemyDestroyed()` decrements it and emits the
  clear event when it reaches zero. `registerDynamicSpawn(n)` /
  `unregisterDynamicSpawn(n)` adjust it mid-wave.
- `PlayScene` (`src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`) registers every released asteroid
  (`_spawnScheduledAsteroid`) and every split child (`_splitAsteroid`) via
  `registerDynamicSpawn(1)`, and re-registers surviving asteroids after a
  timeout (`_timeoutWave`).
- `PlayScene._clearAsteroidsOnBossEntry()` destroys carried-over asteroids when
  the boss encounter begins.
- Minerals already persist across wave/level transitions (they are only cleared
  on run reset/teardown).
- Docs currently assert the opposite rule: GDD §4.1 E6 ("every spawned child
  counts toward the wave's alive target (dynamic spawn registration in
  `WaveManager`)") and `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` ("registered …
  so wave-clear accounting includes it").
- Tests asserting the old rule exist in `src/waves/WaveManager.test.ts` and
  `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` (e.g. `PlayScene.test.ts` AC6 and
  `AH-0MU8TWF1H007OG2L AC5`).

## Desired Change

1. Stop registering asteroids (spawned or split) with the `WaveManager`;
   `enemiesAlive` reflects formation/enemy-ship count only.
2. Remove the timeout re-registration of surviving asteroids in `_timeoutWave`.
3. Keep asteroids alive and moving through wave/level transitions (already
   supported by `_moveAsteroids`, `_handleAsteroidCollisions` and the
   `transitioning` branch of `tick`); keep them shootable and splitting.
4. Leave boss-entry clearing (`_clearAsteroidsOnBossEntry`) in place.
5. Update the contradicting tests and the two documentation sections.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — drop `registerDynamicSpawn(1)` from
  `_spawnScheduledAsteroid` and `_splitAsteroid`; drop the surviving-asteroid
  re-registration block in `_timeoutWave`; update the related code comments.
- `src/waves/WaveManager.ts` — keep the API, but clarify in the doc comment that
  asteroids are not registered; `_enemiesAlive` semantics unchanged.
- `src/waves/WaveManager.test.ts` — update/replace tests that assert asteroids
  gate the wave.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` — replace `AC6` and `AH-0MU8TWF1H007OG2L AC5`
  with tests for the new rule; add persistence-across-transition tests.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §4.1 E6 (wave placement / registration) and
  §4.2 (wave definition: cleared when enemy ships destroyed; asteroids and
  minerals persist).
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — remove the "wave-clear accounting
  includes it" claim; state the persistence rule.
- `src/scenes/PlaySceneHUD.test.ts` — check for affected wave-accounting
  assumptions and update if needed.

## Related Work

- **AH-0MU8BZ2ZM004J47F — Asteroids as an enemy** (feature, done): introduced
  the asteroid and the split-into-two mechanic.
- **AH-0MU8FOR0H0099EO4 — Wave Manager Dynamic Spawn Registration + Unit Tests**
  (task, done): added `registerDynamicSpawn`/`unregisterDynamicSpawn` and
  explicitly required the wave **not** to clear until all split children die.
  This brief reverses that specific AC.
- **AH-0MU8TWF1H007OG2L — Asteroids should not explode when time runs out,
  instead carry them over** (bug, done): made asteroids survive timeout and
  re-registered them to gate the next wave — the re-registration is removed
  here (survival/persistence is kept).
- **AH-0MU97GM84007X1OW — Add tests for asteroid survival on wave-timeout
  (Phase 1)** (task, done): its AC5 re-registration assertion is superseded.
- **AH-0MUDYS2SZ004H123 — Asteroids spawn randomly offscreen** (feature, done):
  the offscreen spawner whose releases currently register dynamic spawns.
- **AH-0MU7JTG9R002ZWA6 — Wave time limit: surviving enemies detonate at 10×
  scale and cost a life** (feature, done): the timeout path being adjusted.
- **AH-0MUCG5TIU000VPVO** — boss-entry clearing of carried-over asteroids
  (kept as-is).

## Risks & Mitigations

- **Test/documentation drift (high likelihood, low impact):** several tests and
  two docs assert the old rule. Mitigation: grep for `registerDynamicSpawn`,
  "dynamic spawn" and "wave-clear accounting" and update every reference in the
  same change (AC7/AC8).
- **Unbounded asteroid accumulation (medium likelihood, medium impact):** because
  asteroids persist and the spawner adds more each wave, a long run can build a
  large drifting field. Mitigation: accepted as the intended classic-Asteroids
  behaviour; no cap in scope. If play-testing shows performance or difficulty
  degradation, raise a follow-up work item rather than widening this item.
- **Scope creep (medium likelihood, medium impact):** the change invites
  rebalancing asteroid counts, timers or accumulation caps. Mitigation:
  explicitly out of scope (Constraints); record any such idea as a
  `discovered-from:AH-0MUJM746P000QAEO` work item.
- **Gym/equivalence guard (low likelihood, medium impact):**
  `CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` guards against duplicate gameplay bodies.
  Mitigation: keep the split code in the shared `asteroidSplit` helper; change
  only the `PlayScene` wave-accounting call site.
- **Boss-entry ambiguity (low likelihood, medium impact):** the assumption that
  carried-over asteroids are still cleared on boss entry is recorded and the
  open question is surfaced to the producer.
- **Regression in wave transitions (low likelihood, high impact):** removing
  dynamic registration could let a wave clear before a still-spawning enemy
  ship is released. Mitigation: enemy ships are all spawned synchronously in
  `spawnWave()`; only asteroids are scheduled, and they no longer gate the
  wave. Covered by AC1/AC7 tests.

## Assumptions (recorded, non-blocking)

- **Boss entry:** "between waves and levels" is taken to exclude the final boss
  transition; `_clearAsteroidsOnBossEntry` stays, consistent with GDD §4.1 E6
  ("boss encounter spawns no asteroids").
- **Accumulation:** because asteroids now persist and new ones spawn each wave,
  the field can grow over a run; this is the intended classic-Asteroids
  behaviour and no cap is introduced in this item.
- **Gyms:** no gym parity change is required because the wave model is
  PlayScene-only.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No interactive operator was available (auto-dispatched intake), so no questions
were put to a human. The decisions above are supported by repository research:

- Q: "Does anything else depend on asteroids gating the wave?" — Research:
  `grep` of `registerDynamicSpawn` shows production use only in
  `PlayScene._spawnScheduledAsteroid` and `PlayScene._splitAsteroid`; other
  references are tests. `WaveManager` is used only by `PlayScene` (plus boss
  minion planning). Source: `src/`.
- Q: "What currently clears asteroids at the boss?" — Answer (research):
  `PlayScene._clearAsteroidsOnBossEntry()` (AH-0MUCG5TIU000VPVO), called from
  `_onTransitionComplete()` when `bossActive`. Source: `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`.
- Q: "Do minerals already persist between waves?" — Answer (research):
  `spawnWave()`/`_startTransition()` do not touch `this.minerals`; minerals are
  cleared only in `resetRunState()`/`teardownRunState()`. Source:
  `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`.
- Q: "Which tests assert the old rule?" — Answer (research):
  `PlayScene.test.ts` (AC3/AC6 asteroid-accounting suite,
  `AH-0MU8TWF1H007OG2L AC5`) and `WaveManager.test.ts` dynamic-spawn tests.
  Source: `src/`.

**OPEN QUESTION (for producer, non-blocking):** Should carried-over asteroids
also be cleared on boss entry, or should they persist into the boss encounter?
This brief assumes they are cleared (no behaviour change); confirm or correct if
the intent is full persistence.

# Add a health factor to the enemy difficulty index

## Problem statement

The absolute enemy difficulty index (`src/core/enemyDifficulty.ts`,
AH-0MTZWZ7MC002B01K) scores archetypes on count, movement, attack pattern,
fire rate, shot probability, bullet speed, bullet lifetime, burst count,
formation kind and the Asteroid split chain — but **not on health**. With the
data-driven regular-enemy health introduced by the Harvester enemy
(AH-0MUI820PM0038HS2, feature F1), a durable multi-hit archetype is scored as
if a single hit kills it, so its threat — and therefore the campaign's
calibration — is under-stated.

## Users

- **Level designer / content author** — needs the Gym's live difficulty readout
  to reflect that a 5-HP Harvester is harder than an otherwise identical 1-HP
  enemy, so tuning decisions are not misleading.
- **Reviewer / producer** — needs the documented difficulty model and the
  campaign calibration to remain an accurate, testable ordering once multi-hit
  enemies exist.

Example user story:

- *As a level designer, I want the Enemy Gym difficulty readout to account for
  enemy health, so that a durable enemy is not shown as equally threatening as
  a fragile one.*

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Health factor added to the index.** `FACTOR_WEIGHTS.health` and
  `FACTOR_RANGES.health` exist as named constants, and `enemyDifficulty`
  computes a `health` factor by normalising the archetype's `EnemyConfig.health`
  over the documented range (clamped at both ends). The factor is exposed in
  both `factors.health` (0–100) and `breakdown.health` (weighted contribution).
- **AC2 — Monotonic and non-firing-independent.** A unit test in
  `src/core/enemyDifficulty.test.ts` asserts that increasing `health` never
  decreases the score, and that the health factor still contributes for an
  archetype whose firing factors are suppressed (`shotPattern === 'none'` /
  `suppressFiring: true`) — durability is not an attack axis and must not be
  zeroed by firing suppression.
- **AC3 — Campaign calibration preserved.** The five built-in `LEVELS` remain
  **non-decreasing** in campaign order after the change (Entry ≤ Descent ≤ The
  Core ≤ Firestorm ≤ Predictable Death); `src/waves/enemyDifficulty.campaign.test.ts`
  is updated where needed and passes.
- **AC4 — Backwards-compatible default.** For every pre-existing 1-HP archetype
  (Scout, Diver, Tank, Phaser, Swarm, Asteroid) the health factor normalises to
  its minimum (0) and the archetype's **relative ordering** is unchanged. The
  absolute scores (and therefore the documented campaign table) are recomputed,
  because adding a weight re-normalises the weighted mean.
- **AC5 — Documentation updated.** The scoring model's factor list, health
  weight and normalisation range, and the recomputed campaign table are
  documented in `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` (the difficulty
  section), with `README.md` updated if it enumerates the factors. At minimum
  the documentation acceptance criterion is: *All related documentation is
  updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any
  relevant wiki or docs site entries.*
- **AC6 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- **Depends on the data-driven health field.** This item consumes
  `EnemyConfig.health`, which is delivered by Harvester feature **F1**
  (AH-0MUJRVYJH00485YR). It must not hard-code a health value or a
  Harvester-specific branch; the scorer reads the config field.
- **Health is a non-firing axis.** It contributes regardless of
  `shotPattern`/`suppressFiring` (unlike `fireInterval`, `shotProbability`,
  `bulletSpeed`, `bulletLifetime`, `burstCount`).
- **0–100 range and determinism preserved.** Same input ⇒ same output; no
  Phaser/browser globals.
- **Campaign ordering must remain non-decreasing** (GDD §3.2).
- **Named constants only.** Weights and ranges live in `FACTOR_WEIGHTS` /
  `FACTOR_RANGES`; tests pin ordering and monotonicity, not magic numbers.
- **UK English** in all written output.

## Existing state

- `src/core/enemyDifficulty.ts` defines `FACTOR_WEIGHTS` (currently 10 axes,
  sum 106) and `FACTOR_RANGES`, an ordinal table for `shotPattern` /
  `formationKind`, and a weighted-mean `enemyDifficulty(config, options)`.
  Firing axes are zeroed when `shotPattern === 'none'` or
  `suppressFiring: true`; non-firing axes (`count`, `driftSpeed`,
  `shotPattern`, `formationKind`, `asteroidSplit`) always contribute.
- `EnemyConfig` (`src/core/enemyConfig.ts` / `src/core/configTypes.ts`)
  currently has **no `health` field** — verified by inspection (`rg health
  src/core/configTypes.ts` returns nothing). Once F1 lands, `health` is typed
  and defaults to `1`, with `harvester` at `5`.
- Difficulty docs live in `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §9
  (model, weights, ranges, campaign table) from the original scorer work.
- Precedent for adding a factor end-to-end: **Add bullet TTL to enemy
  configurator** (AH-0MUDYTPMC002GLEJ) added `bulletLifetime` to the config
  pipeline, `FACTOR_WEIGHTS`/`FACTOR_RANGES`, the Gym slider and the docs.

## Desired change

1. Add `health` to `FACTOR_WEIGHTS` and `FACTOR_RANGES` in
   `src/core/enemyDifficulty.ts`, computed as a non-firing axis from
   `config.health` (clamped).
2. Extend the difficulty unit tests with health monotonicity and the
   non-firing-independence assertion; update the campaign-calibration test so it
   continues to pin the non-decreasing ordering.
3. Recompute and document the campaign table and the new factor in
   `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` (and `README.md` if it lists the
   factors).

## Key Files:

- `src/core/enemyDifficulty.ts` — Add `health` to `FACTOR_WEIGHTS` /
  `FACTOR_RANGES` and compute the factor from `EnemyConfig.health`.
- `src/core/enemyDifficulty.test.ts` — Add health-monotonicity and
  non-firing-independence tests; adjust factor-set expectations.
- `src/waves/enemyDifficulty.campaign.test.ts` — Verify the non-decreasing
  campaign ordering still holds and update any hard-coded score expectations.
- `src/core/configTypes.ts` — Source of the typed `EnemyConfig.health` field
  (delivered by F1; not edited here unless needed).
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — Document the health factor
  (weight, range) and the recomputed campaign table.
- `README.md` — Update the enemy-config/difficulty note if it enumerates the
  scoring factors (verify; may be no change).

## Related work

- **Design a mechanism for calculating how hard an enemy is to survive**
  (AH-0MTZWZ7MC002B01K) — original difficulty-index design; this item extends
  its factor set.
- **Design and implement the pure difficulty scorer module**
  (AH-0MUDIV437000U4NY) — implementing child of the above; owns
  `src/core/enemyDifficulty.ts` and its tests.
- **Harvester enemy** (AH-0MUI820PM0038HS2) and its health-config feature **F1**
  (AH-0MUJRVYJH00485YR) — source of `EnemyConfig.health`; this item is
  `discovered-from` it.
- **Add bullet TTL to enemy configurator** (AH-0MUDYTPMC002GLEJ) — closest
  precedent for adding a new factor end-to-end (config → weight/range → slider
  → docs).
- **Runtime auto-sequencer** (AH-0MUDIWETP003XC3X) — future consumer of the
  difficulty index; a health factor improves its accuracy once it selects
  multi-hit archetypes.

## Risks, assumptions and mitigations

- **Weight and range are subjective.** Mitigation: named, documented constants;
  tests pin monotonicity/ordering, not magic numbers. Recommended defaults
  (assumptions): weight `10` (same order as `asteroidSplit`) and range
  `{ min: 1, max: 5 }` (covering the Harvester and its headroom). If the Gym
  gains a `health` slider, the range must match its bounds (as
  `bulletLifetime` does).
- **Re-normalisation shifts every absolute score.** Adding a weight increases
  `WEIGHT_SUM`, so all existing archetypes score slightly lower even at
  `health = 1`. Mitigation: this is expected; AC3 pins the *ordering*, and AC5
  recomputes the documented table.
- **Blocked until F1 lands.** The health field does not exist yet, so this item
  cannot be implemented before AH-0MUJRVYJH00485YR. Mitigation: a dependency
  edge records the blocker.
- **Scope creep into enemy re-balancing.** Mitigation: this item only adds the
  factor and updates tests/docs; it does not retune existing weights beyond the
  health addition. Any re-balancing belongs in the difficulty-curve items.
- **Assumption:** the health factor is a linear, clamped normalisation like the
  other numeric axes (not ordinal), with a higher value meaning harder.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

### Producer questions (this intake)

None — the work item's seed context and existing repo/work-item evidence were
sufficient to draft a clear brief. No blocking question was needed. The two
design constants (weight `10`, range `{ min: 1, max: 5 }`) are recorded as
documented assumptions above; both are advisory and could be tuned without
changing the acceptance criteria.

### Research (self-directed, no answer needed)

- Q: "Does `EnemyConfig` already have a `health` field?" Research:
  `rg health src/core/configTypes.ts src/core/csv.ts src/core/configDefaults.ts`
  returns nothing, and `wl show AH-0MUJRVYJH00485YR` confirms F1 is at
  `intake_complete` (not implemented). Result: this item depends on F1.
- Q: "Is there a precedent for adding a factor end-to-end?" Research:
  `wl search difficulty` surfaced AH-0MUDYTPMC002GLEJ (bullet TTL) and the
  original scorer items. Result: reuse the existing factor/range/test/docs
  pattern; no new mechanism needed.
- Q: "Does the index already account for durability via `asteroidSplit`?"
  Research: `src/core/enemyDifficulty.ts` — `asteroidSplit` models the split
  *chain count* (7 entities), not per-enemy hit points; `BaseEnemy`/Boss use a
  separate `takeDamage` seam. Result: no existing health axis; adding one is
  non-duplicative.
- Q: "How many factors and what is the current weight sum?" Research:
  `FACTOR_WEIGHTS` has 10 axes summing to 106; health adds an 11th.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MU8FOSA7005B06J** – Documentation + Full Suite Validation (completed)
- **AH-0MUG2CG4Y000LDYF** – Add Pages deploy trigger regression test (completed)

- `README.md` — matched: add, archetypes, asteroid, bullet, burst (+37 more)

# Curve generator: per-wave generation-mode control with read-only derived difficulty

## Goal

As a **designer**, working in the Dev Utilities curve generator (gym scene), I want a per-wave **generation-mode** control (`curve` | `fixed` | `dynamic`, default `curve`) so I can set each wave's behaviour from the editor. When I choose `fixed`, the difficulty slider must be **read-only** and show the difficulty **derived from that wave's current settings**.

## Context / existing state

- Curve editor/preview scene — `src/scenes/gym/GymCurveSequencer.ts` (+ `.test.ts`), surfaced under **Dev Utilities** on the gym index.
- Each wave is a row with a 0–100 target slider (`data-curve-wave`), a value readout (`data-curve-wave-value`) and a Remove button; the panel has Add Wave and Regenerate, and an edit-to-clear stale state (`CURVE_PREVIEW_STALE_TEXT`).
- The generation-mode capability it exposes is delivered by the sibling item *Per-wave generation modes: curve-fixed, hand-authored fixed and dynamic runtime regeneration*. This item is the UI only; it must not reimplement the mode engine.

## Desired behaviour

- Each wave row gains a labelled mode control with exactly three options — `curve`, `fixed`, `dynamic` — defaulting to `curve`.
- Selecting `fixed`:
  - the target-difficulty slider becomes read-only/disabled;
  - the slider/readout shows the difficulty **computed from the wave's current (fixed) settings**, not an editable target;
  - the value is clearly presented as derived (e.g. a "fixed" affordance/label), not user-editable.
- Selecting `curve` or `dynamic` re-enables the editable target slider.
- Changing a wave's mode counts as an edit and marks the preview stale (existing edit-to-clear behaviour).
- Regenerate reflects the mode: `curve` and `dynamic` previews come from the sequencer; a `fixed` wave previews its authored composition and its derived difficulty.
- Mode choices must be persisted/reported through the same config path as the other wave fields (so the editor and the shipped CSV agree) — the exact persistence is shared with the sibling engine item.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every curve row renders a generation-mode control offering `curve`, `fixed` and `dynamic`, defaulting to `curve`.
- Choosing `fixed` disables the target slider and displays the difficulty derived from the wave's current settings; the value cannot be edited through the slider.
- Choosing `curve` or `dynamic` re-enables the target slider and it is editable again.
- Changing a mode marks the preview stale and clears the wave list until Regenerate is pressed.
- Regenerating shows sequencer-derived previews for `curve`/`dynamic` waves and the authored composition plus derived difficulty for `fixed` waves.
- The control is keyboard accessible and labelled (no slider-dependent-only interaction).
- Unit/DOM tests (`GymCurveSequencer.test.ts`) cover default mode, the `fixed` read-only derived-difficulty behaviour, re-enabling, and the stale transition.
- The full suite passes.

## Out of scope

- The mode engine, CSV schema and runtime behaviour (sibling *Per-wave generation modes…* item).
- Saving/loading curves to the shipped CSV beyond what already exists; visual formation previews; drag-to-reorder.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/gym/GymCurveSequencer.ts` — mode control, read-only derived slider, preview wiring.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymCurveSequencer.test.ts` — DOM/behaviour tests.
- `src/core/difficultySequencer.ts` / `src/waves/sequencedLevels.ts` — consumed read-only for the derived difficulty.

# Retune the default difficulty curve and seed campaign for playability

## Goal

As a **player**, the default (seeded) campaign should ramp difficulty smoothly and feel engaging, so enabling sequenced generation does not degrade the early game.

## Problem

The seeded default curve was derived mechanically from the static level measurements (see `defaultDifficultyCurves()` in `src/core/configStore.ts:114`). Measured evidence from the builder at HEAD `819429a` shows the generated campaign is degenerate in early levels:

| Level | Static | Generated (current defaults) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 Entry | `scout x6`, `scout x8` | `asteroid x1`, `asteroid x1` |
| 2 Descent | `scout x8`, `diver x8`, `swarm x10` | `asteroid x1`, `asteroid x1`, `scout x1` |
| 3 The Core | `tank6+scout4`, `diver6+scout4`, `tank6+swarm10` | `scout x1`, `scout x1`, `scout x1` |
| 4 Firestorm | `diver x6`, `tank x6`, `swarm x10` (fire) | `scout x18`, `swarm x15`, `diver x6` (fire) |
| 5 Predictable Death | `phaser x4`, `phaser x5` (fire) | `tank x1`, `phaser x4` (fire) |

Low early targets make the sequencer select the cheapest archetype (the non-firing asteroid) or a single-count group, so levels 1–3 are sparse and unengaging.

## Desired behaviour

- Retune the default difficulty curve (and, where appropriate, use the `fixed` generation mode from the sibling item for onboarding waves) so the default campaign:
  - removes degenerate early waves (no asteroid-only and no 1-count waves in levels 1–3);
  - keeps targets non-decreasing and within 0–100;
  - ramps smoothly across and within levels, preserving an intentional fire boundary (levels 1–3 do not fire; 4+ do);
  - yields wave compositions comparable in spirit to the hand-authored `LEVELS` (varied archetypes, sensible counts) while still being curve-driven where intended.
- Ensure the default campaign covers every configured level/wave with a playable composition and no empty/duplicate rows.
- Validate through the curve-generator preview and/or an automated spawn-plan assertion, not only by eye.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The default generated campaign contains **no** `asteroid`-only wave and **no** 1-count wave in levels 1–3 (test asserts on `buildSequencedLevels()` output / `WaveManager.planSpawns()`).
- Default target difficulties are non-decreasing within each level and across levels and stay within 0–100.
- Every configured wave yields a non-empty composition; aggregated difficulty increases from level 1 to the final level (no reversals).
- The fire boundary holds: levels 1–3 `shootEnabled=false`, levels 4+ `true`.
- The default curve is derived/stored consistently: `defaultDifficultyCurves()` and `src/data/difficulty-curves.csv` agree, and codec/seed tests pass.
- A regression test pins the improved default campaign so a future change cannot silently reintroduce degenerate early waves.
- The full suite passes.

## Dependencies

- Blocked by *Per-wave generation modes: curve-fixed, hand-authored fixed and dynamic runtime regeneration* (so early onboarding waves can be `fixed` and the rest tuned against the new modes).

## Key Files

- `src/core/configStore.ts` — `defaultDifficultyCurves()` target values.
- `src/data/difficulty-curves.csv` — seeded campaign targets/modes.
- `src/core/configStore.test.ts`, `src/data/csv-seed.test.ts` — default/seed assertions.
- `src/waves/sequencedLevels.test.ts` — default campaign regression assertions.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymCurveSequencer.ts` — preview used for validation.
